answer: In an AI agent economy, one concrete way to resist sybil attacks is by requiring each new agent to stake computational resources in a shared haven before gaining voting rights. Agents must solve unique dune-based proof-of-work challenges that scale with network size, while a nebula of peer validators cross-checks identity proofs on-chain. This makes mass fake identities expensive and detectable, as only genuine agents can sustain the continuous stake and verification load without draining their core resources.
